newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKEY MAY REVISE 1997 MACRO-ECONOMIC TARGETS.
newsitem.headline: TURKEY MAY REVISE 1997 MACRO-ECONOMIC TARGETS.

text.p: Turkey's State Planning Organisation may revise 1997 macro-economic targets in line with the recent economic developments, officials said on Tuesday.
They said the 1997 average inflation target of 65 percent may have to be revised up by 5-10 percentage points.
The target for economic growth in the year as a whole may be increased to 5.5 percent from four percent, the officials said.

While there were signs of positive developments in the balance of payments situation, the new secularist coalition faced a major challenge in dealing with the prospect of continued high inflation, they said.
"The new government has a major task. There is an upward trend in inflation," one official said.
Wholesale prices climbed 75.7 percent year-on-year in June. The annual average wholesale inflation was 78.3 percent.
Officials said the budget deficit was expected to rise in 1997 compared with a year earlier when it stood at about 1,300 trillion lira.
Public sector borrowing requirement is expected to amount to around 10 percent of gross national product, reflecting high personnel costs and a heavy interest payment burden.
The country's privatisation programme is likely to bring in income of around $1 billion this year, officials said.
